body:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render the 4 Winning Packet graphics cards with PIL. 1080x1350."""
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

OUT = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/your_files/graphics")
W, H = 1080, 1350
BG = (7, 11, 22)
CYAN = (34, 211, 238)
PINK = (232, 121, 249)
ROSE = (251, 113, 133)
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
MUT = (148, 163, 184)
DIMM = (100, 116, 139)
DARKMUT = (71, 85, 105)

def font(size, bold=False):
    name = "DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf" if bold else "DejaVuSans.ttf"
    for p in [f"/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/{name}", f"/usr/share/fonts/{name}"]:
        if os.path.exists(p):
            return ImageFont.truetype(p, size)
    return ImageFont.load_default()

def glow_bg(accent):
    img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
    ov = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
    # soft top glow
    for i in range(60):
        a = int(28 * (1 - i / 60))
        d.ellipse([-500 + i*8, -700 + i*8, W + 500 - i*8, 500 - i*4],
                  fill=accent + (a,))
    img = Image.alpha_composite(img.convert("RGBA"), ov).convert("RGB")
    return img

def kicker(d, y, text, color):
    d.text((70, y), text, font=font(26, True), fill=color)
    return y + 48

def title(d, y, text, size=84):
    f = font(size, True)
    d.text((70, y), text, font=f, fill=WHITE)
    # measure lines
    lines = text.split("\n")
    return y + int(size * 1.15 * len(lines)) + 8

def sub(d, y, text):
    d.text((70, y), text, font=font(30), fill=MUT)
    return y + 52

def brand(d):
    f = font(24)
    d.text((70, H - 80), "GALAXY SPORTS EDGE", font=f, fill=DARKMUT)
    t = "WE DETECT. YOU DECIDE."
    bb = d.textbbox((0, 0), t, font=f)
    d.text((W - 70 - (bb[2] - bb[0]), H - 80), t, font=f, fill=DARKMUT)

def card_box(img, y, h):
    ov = Image.new("RGBA", img.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
    d.rounded_rectangle([60, y, W - 60, y + h], radius=22,
                        fill=(148, 163, 184, 18), outline=(148, 163, 184, 46), width=2)
    img.paste(Image.alpha_composite(img.convert("RGBA"), ov).convert("RGB"))
    return ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# ---------- 1. THE BOARD ----------
img = glow_bg(CYAN); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
y = 120
y = kicker(d, y, "THE WINNING PACKET \u00b7 WEEK 2", CYAN)
y = title(d, y, "THE BOARD")
y = sub(d, y, "The exact lineup. No paywall.")
rows = [
    ("QB", "C.J. Stroud", "HOU", "$5,500"),
    ("RB", "Derrick Henry", "BAL", "$7,200"),
    ("RB", "D'Andre Swift", "CHI", "$6,300"),
    ("WR", "Jaxon Smith-Njigba", "SEA", "$8,100"),
    ("WR", "DK Metcalf", "PIT", "$5,200"),
    ("WR", "Xavier Hutchinson", "HOU", "$3,500"),
    ("TE", "Dalton Schultz", "HOU", "$3,200"),
    ("FLEX", "Christian McCaffrey", "SF", "$8,000"),
    ("DST", "Jacksonville", "JAX", "$2,400"),
]
y += 10
for pos, name, team, sal in rows:
    d.text((70, y), pos, font=font(24, True), fill=CYAN)
    d.text((200, y - 2), name, font=font(30, True), fill=WHITE)
    nw = d.textbbox((0, 0), name, font=font(30, True))[2]
    d.text((200 + nw + 14, y + 2), team, font=font(28), fill=MUT)
    sw = d.textbbox((0, 0), sal, font=font(30, True))[2]
    d.text((W - 70 - sw, y - 2), sal, font=font(30, True), fill=(226, 232, 240))
    y += 62
    d.line([70, y - 12, W - 70, y - 12], fill=(148, 163, 184, 40), width=1)
y += 26
d.text((70, y), "TOTAL", font=font(34, True), fill=WHITE)
t2 = "$49,400 / $50,000"
sw = d.textbbox((0, 0), t2, font=font(34, True))[2]
d.text((W - 70 - sw, y), t2, font=font(34, True), fill=CYAN)
y += 60
d.text((70, y), "Salaries via DraftKings \u00b7 15-game slate", font=font(24), fill=DIMM)
brand(d)
img.save(f"{OUT}/packet-lineup.png")

# ---------- 2. THE STACK ----------
img = glow_bg(PINK); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
y = 120
y = kicker(d, y, "THE WINNING PACKET \u00b7 WEEK 2", PINK)
y = title(d, y, "THE STACK")
y = sub(d, y, "One stack wins tournaments. This is ours.")
y += 8
stack = [
    ("QB \u00b7 $5,500", "C.J. Stroud", "Home vs Cincinnati. Nico Collins is out. Somebody has to catch those passes."),
    ("WR \u00b7 $3,500", "Xavier Hutchinson", "A star's routes at minimum price. The pricing department fell asleep."),
    ("TE \u00b7 $3,200", "Dalton Schultz", "74% of routes, 18% first-read share vs the worst TE defense in football."),
]
for p, n, desc in stack:
    d = card_box(img, y, 218)
    d.text((100, y + 26), p, font=font(26, True), fill=PINK)
    d.text((100, y + 62), n, font=font(44, True), fill=WHITE)
    # wrap desc
    words, lines, cur = desc.split(), [], ""
    for w in words:
        t = (cur + " " + w).strip()
        if d.textbbox((0, 0), t, font=font(29))[2] < 840:
            cur = t
        else:
            lines.append(cur); cur = w
    lines.append(cur)
    ly = y + 122
    for ln in lines[:2]:
        d.text((100, ly), ln, font=font(29), fill=(203, 213, 225)); ly += 40
    y += 218 + 26
y += 14
d = card_box(img, y, 120)
d.text((100, y + 38), "COMBINED", font=font(30, True), fill=MUT)
t2 = "$12,200"
sw = d.textbbox((0, 0), t2, font=font(56, True))[2]
d.text((W - 100 - sw, y + 24), t2, font=font(56, True), fill=CYAN)
brand(d)
img.save(f"{OUT}/packet-stack.png")

# ---------- 3. THE SIGNAL ----------
img = glow_bg(CYAN); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
y = 120
y = kicker(d, y, "THE WINNING PACKET \u00b7 WEEK 2", CYAN)
y = title(d, y, "THE SIGNAL")
y = sub(d, y, "What our lab actually found. Percentiles, not opinions.")
y += 8
edges = [
    ("JAX pass defense vs DEN", "100th", 100, CYAN, "Denver's pass offense: 9.7. That's why Jacksonville is our defense."),
    ("BAL pass defense vs NO", "96.8th", 96.8, CYAN, "Saints can't throw on them. Henry runs clock all second half."),
    ("SF offense vs MIA", "93rd", 93, CYAN, "Miami's defense: 12th. The CMC game, in 72 and clear."),
    ("Chargers INT luck (fade)", "+7.11", 88, ROSE, "Takeaways that already happened. We passed. Our optimizer disagreed."),
]
for lab, val, pct, col, note in edges:
    d.text((70, y), lab, font=font(28, True), fill=WHITE)
    vw = d.textbbox((0, 0), val, font=font(28, True))[2]
    d.text((W - 70 - vw, y), val, font=font(28, True), fill=col)
    y += 52
    d.rounded_rectangle([70, y, W - 70, y + 26], radius=13, fill=(148, 163, 184, 36))
    fw = int((W - 140) * pct / 100)
    d.rounded_rectangle([70, y, 70 + fw, y + 26], radius=13, fill=col)
    y += 40
    d.text((70, y), note, font=font(25), fill=MUT)
    y += 62
y += 10
d.text((70, y), "Source: GSE lab unit-matchup + turnover-luck tables", font=font(24), fill=DIMM)
brand(d)
img.save(f"{OUT}/packet-edges.png")

# ---------- 4. WHAT WE PASSED ON ----------
img = glow_bg(ROSE); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
y = 120
y = kicker(d, y, "THE WINNING PACKET \u00b7 WEEK 2", ROSE)
y = title(d, y, "WHAT WE\nPASSED ON", size=76)
d.text((70, y), "A pass is not a blank. It is the finding.", font=font(28), fill=(226, 232, 240))
y += 70
fades = [
    ("Chargers DST", "PASS", "+7.11 interceptions of pure luck. You're paying for takeaways that already happened."),
    ("Chris Olave", "PASS", "Hamstring, game-time decision, vs a 96th-percentile pass defense. A donation, not a risk."),
    ("Terry McLaurin", "PASS", "Every show loves him. Our role data says mirage. Paying for the name on the jersey."),
]
for n, tag, desc in fades:
    d = card_box(img, y, 210)
    d.text((100, y + 26), n, font=font(40, True), fill=WHITE)
    nw = d.textbbox((0, 0), n, font=font(40, True))[2]
    d.text((100 + nw + 18, y + 34), "\u00b7 " + tag, font=font(28, True), fill=ROSE)
    words, lines, cur = desc.split(), [], ""
    for w in words:
        t = (cur + " " + w).strip()
        if d.textbbox((0, 0), t, font=font(28))[2] < 840:
            cur = t
        else:
            lines.append(cur); cur = w
    lines.append(cur)
    ly = y + 96
    for ln in lines[:2]:
        d.text((100, ly), ln, font=font(28), fill=(203, 213, 225)); ly += 42
    y += 210 + 26
brand(d)
img.save(f"{OUT}/packet-passed.png")

print("done:", sorted(f for f in os.listdir(OUT) if f.startswith("packet-") and f.endswith(".png")))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render 6 GSE Week 2 cards from GSE-Week2-Lineup-Card.pdf. 1080x1350. PIL only."""
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

OUT = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/your_files/graphics")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
W, H = 1080, 1350
BG = (7, 11, 22)
CYAN = (34, 211, 238)
VIOLET = (168, 85, 247)
GREEN = (52, 211, 153)
ROSE = (251, 113, 133)
AMBER = (251, 191, 36)
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
MUT = (148, 163, 184)
DIMM = (100, 116, 139)
DARKMUT = (71, 85, 105)

def font(size, bold=False):
    name = "DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf" if bold else "DejaVuSans.ttf"
    for p in [f"/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/{name}"]:
        if os.path.exists(p):
            return ImageFont.truetype(p, size)
    return ImageFont.load_default()

def base(accent):
    img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
    ov = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
    for i in range(60):
        a = int(26 * (1 - i / 60))
        d.ellipse([-500 + i*8, -700 + i*8, W + 500 - i*8, 500 - i*4], fill=accent + (a,))
    return Image.alpha_composite(img.convert("RGBA"), ov).convert("RGB")

def brand(d):
    f = font(24)
    d.text((70, H - 80), "GALAXY SPORTS EDGE", font=f, fill=DARKMUT)
    t = "WE DETECT. YOU DECIDE."
    bb = d.textbbox((0, 0), t, font=f)
    d.text((W - 70 - (bb[2] - bb[0]), H - 80), t, font=f, fill=DARKMUT)

def kicker(d, y, text, color=CYAN):
    d.text((70, y), text, font=font(26, True), fill=color)
    return y + 52

def wrap(d, text, fnt, maxw):
    words, lines, cur = text.split(), [], ""
    for w in words:
        t = (cur + " " + w).strip()
        if d.textbbox((0, 0), t, font=fnt)[2] < maxw:
            cur = t
        else:
            lines.append(cur); cur = w
    if cur: lines.append(cur)
    return lines

def box(img, y, h, accent=MUT):
    ov = Image.new("RGBA", img.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
    d.rounded_rectangle([60, y, W - 60, y + h], radius=22,
                        fill=(148, 163, 184, 18), outline=(148, 163, 184, 46), width=2)
    img.paste(Image.alpha_composite(img.convert("RGBA"), ov).convert("RGB"))
    return ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# ============ 1. HERO ============
img = base(VIOLET); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
y = 300
d.text((70, y), "GALAXY", font=font(120, True), fill=WHITE); y += 135
d.text((70, y), "SPORTS EDGE", font=font(120, True), fill=CYAN); y += 170
d.text((70, y), "NFL WEEK 2 — DRAFTKINGS CLASSIC", font=font(34, True), fill=WHITE); y += 70
d.text((70, y), "We detect. You decide.", font=font(36), fill=MUT); y += 90
d.text((70, y), "15-game Sun-Mon slate · Lock 12:00 PM CDT", font=font(30), fill=DIMM); y += 60
d.text((70, y), "@GalaxySportsHQ · galaxysportsedge.com", font=font(30), fill=DIMM)
brand(d)
img.save(f"{OUT}/gse-hero.png")

# ============ LINEUP CARD BUILDER ============
def lineup_card(fname, knum, ktitle, accent, rows, thesis_lines, note=None):
    img = base(accent); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    y = 90
    y = kicker(d, y, f"GALAXY SPORTS EDGE · WEEK 2 · LINEUP {knum}", accent)
    d.text((70, y), ktitle, font=font(64, True), fill=WHITE); y += 92
    d.text((70, y), "$50,000 cap-exact · LineStar 15-game ownership", font=font(28), fill=MUT); y += 62
    # header
    d.text((70, y), "POS", font=font(22, True), fill=DIMM)
    d.text((180, y), "PLAYER", font=font(22, True), fill=DIMM)
    for lbl, x in (("SALARY", W - 330), ("OWN", W - 170)):
        bb = d.textbbox((0, 0), lbl, font=font(22, True))
        d.text((x - (bb[2]-bb[0]), y), lbl, font=font(22, True), fill=DIMM)
    y += 40
    d.line([70, y, W-70, y], fill=(148,163,184,60), width=2); y += 18
    for pos, name, team, opp, sal, own in rows:
        d.text((70, y), pos, font=font(24, True), fill=accent)
        d.text((180, y - 2), name, font=font(29, True), fill=WHITE)
        nw = d.textbbox((0, 0), name, font=font(29, True))[2]
        d.text((180 + nw + 12, y + 3), f"{team} vs {opp}", font=font(24), fill=MUT)
        for val, x in ((sal, W - 240), (own, W - 70)):
            bb = d.textbbox((0, 0), val, font=font(28, True))
            d.text((x - (bb[2]-bb[0]), y - 2), val, font=font(28, True), fill=(226,232,240))
        y += 58
        d.line([70, y - 10, W - 70, y - 10], fill=(148,163,184,28), width=1)
    y += 8
    d = box(img, y, 190, accent)
    ty = y + 28
    for i, ln in enumerate(thesis_lines):
        d.text((100, ty), ln, font=font(28, True) if i == 0 else font(28), fill=WHITE if i == 0 else (203,213,225))
        ty += 44
    if note:
        d.text((100, ty + 6), note, font=font(24), fill=AMBER)
    brand(d)
    img.save(f"{OUT}/{fname}")

lineup_a = [
    ("QB", "Jayden Daniels", "WAS", "DAL", "$6,300", "9.2%"),
    ("RB", "Bijan Robinson", "ATL", "CAR", "$8,200", "28.6%"),
    ("RB", "Ashton Jeanty", "LV", "LAC", "$6,800", "5.8%"),
    ("WR", "Stefon Diggs", "WAS", "DAL", "$5,300", "8.8%"),
    ("WR", "Terry McLaurin", "WAS", "DAL", "$5,200", "5.1%"),
    ("WR", "DK Metcalf", "PIT", "NE", "$5,200", "1.3%"),
    ("TE", "Dalton Schultz", "HOU", "CIN", "$3,200", "15.6%"),
    ("FLX", "Kenneth Walker III", "KC", "IND", "$6,500", "5.1%"),
    ("DST", "Ravens", "BAL", "NO", "$3,300", "10.0%"),
]
lineup_card("gse-lineup-a.png", "A", "THE ONE WE'D FIRE", CYAN, lineup_a,
    ["THE THESIS",
     "Dallas pass defense: 3.2nd percentile. Worst in our lab.",
     "Minus two starters. WAS gets them in the 50.5-total game, indoors."])

lineup_b = [
    ("QB", "Dak Prescott", "DAL", "WAS", "$6,400", "9.7%"),
    ("RB", "Kenneth Walker III", "KC", "IND", "$6,500", "5.1%"),
    ("RB", "Javonte Williams", "DAL", "WAS", "$6,400", "26.0%"),
    ("WR", "CeeDee Lamb", "DAL", "WAS", "$7,300", "15%"),
    ("WR", "George Pickens", "DAL", "WAS", "$6,300", "21.4%"),
    ("WR", "DK Metcalf", "PIT", "NE", "$5,200", "1.3%"),
    ("TE", "Isaiah Likely", "NYG", "LAR", "$4,500", "4.1%"),
    ("FLX", "Jake Ferguson", "DAL", "WAS", "$3,800", "2.4%"),
    ("DST", "Buccaneers", "TB", "CLE", "$3,600", "12.0%"),
]
lineup_card("gse-lineup-b.png", "B", "MAX CEILING", VIOLET, lineup_b,
    ["THE PIVOT",
     "Five pieces of the 50.5 game. Every Dallas TD pays three times.",
     "One entry: fire A for the best shot, B for the highest score."],
    note="Honest caveat: the Dallas stack is the slate's most-duplicated correlation.")

# ============ 4. SLATE MATRIX ============
img = base(GREEN); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
y = 110
y = kicker(d, y, "GALAXY SPORTS EDGE · WEEK 2", GREEN)
d.text((70, y), "SLATE MATRIX", font=font(72, True), fill=WHITE); y += 105
d.text((70, y), "Role vs ownership. GSE proprietary ratings.", font=font(28), fill=MUT); y += 80
cols = [70, 330, 640, 800]
for lbl, x in zip(["PLAYER", "ROLE", "OWN%", "GSE RATING"], cols):
    d.text((x, y), lbl, font=font(22, True), fill=DIMM)
y += 42
d.line([70, y, W-70, y], fill=(148,163,184,60), width=2); y += 26
mrows = [
    ("Metcalf, DK", "WR1 (No Pittman)", "1.3%", "AAA+ LEVERAGE", GREEN, False),
    ("Schultz, Dalton", "Only healthy target", "15.6%", "SALARY GLITCH ($3.2K)", AMBER, False),
    ("Nacua, Puka", "DNP / Doubtful MNF", "--", "AUTO-ZERO TRAP", ROSE, True),
]
for name, role, own, rate, col, crossed in mrows:
    d.text((cols[0], y), name, font=font(32, True), fill=WHITE)
    d.text((cols[1], y + 6), role, font=font(26), fill=MUT)
    d.text((cols[2], y), own, font=font(32, True), fill=WHITE)
    d.text((cols[3], y + 6), rate, font=font(26, True), fill=col)
    if crossed:
        d.line([cols[0]-10, y+22, W-70, y+22], fill=ROSE, width=6)
        d.line([cols[0]-10, y+30, W-70, y+30], fill=ROSE, width=4)
    y += 96
    d.line([70, y - 22, W - 70, y - 22], fill=(148,163,184,28), width=1)
y += 40
d = box(img, y, 150)
for i, ln in enumerate(["1.3% owned with Pittman OUT and NE's CB1 OUT is criminal.",
                        "Puka is doubtful Monday night. You lock Sunday at noon."]):
    d.text((100, y + 30 + i*44), ln, font=font(28), fill=(203,213,225))
brand(d)
img.save(f"{OUT}/gse-matrix.png")

# ============ 5. LEVERAGE SHEET ============
img = base(ROSE); d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
y = 110
y = kicker(d, y, "GALAXY SPORTS EDGE · WEEK 2", ROSE)
d.text((70, y), "LEVERAGE SHEET", font=font(72, True), fill=WHITE); y += 110
d = box(img, y, 300)
d.text((100, y + 30), "28.4%", font=font(96, True), fill=ROSE)
d.text((100, y + 140), "TRAP", font=font(72, True), fill=WHITE)
d.text((100, y + 226), "Aaron Jones. Soldier Field: 30 mph gusts + 100% rain. FADE.",
       font=font(28), fill=MUT)
y += 330
d = box(img, y, 300)
d.text((100, y + 30), "5%", font=font(96, True), fill=GREEN)
d.text((100, y + 140), "UNTOUCHED", font=font(72, True), fill=WHITE)
d.text((100, y + 226), "Ashton Jeanty. 87% XFP share vs the Chargers. RUN IT.",
       font=font(28), fill=MUT)
y += 330
d.text((70, y), "Chalk you can smell from the parking lot vs the role nobody priced.",
       font=font(28), fill=MUT)
brand(d)

A breakout star in 2025, Drake Maye
has struggled so far in 2026. He had 178 passing yards, one touchdown and three interceptions in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks, and he had 208 passing yards, no touchdowns and one interception in a Week 2 win over the Steelers. I’m not especially concerned. Seattle has the best pass defense in the league, so I’m giving Maye a mulligan for the poor Week 1 results. Maye threw only 22 passes against the Steelers last week and averaged 9.5 yards per attempt. The perception is that he had a poor game, but he simply didn’t need to do much because the Steelers’ offense was so inept. Maye showed last season that he’s one of the best pure passers in the league, and he adds rushing value. Maye has 11 carries for 64 yards. Start Maye with confidence this week against the Jaguars even though Patriots WR AJ Brown remains out with an ankle injury.
Tyler Shough
ranks second in the league in pass attempts (93), first in completions (62) and first in passing yards (662). Shough’s 410-yard day against the Lions in Week 1 was fueled by a pass-happy game script, with the Saints falling into an early 21-0 hole, and it’s worth noting that the Detroit pass defense has been a train wreck. But Saints head coach Kellen Moore loves to push the pace, and Shough adds value with his legs as well. He has 31 rushing yards and a touchdown so far this season. Shough’s Week 2 matchup against the Raiders isn’t as favorable as it would seem. Las Vegas has the second-lowest opponent passer rating (63.2) behind only Seattle, and the Raiders have allowed only one TD pass. I’m slightly below consensus on Shough, ranking him as a borderline low-end QB1/high-end QB2.
Geno Smith
is a viable matchup-based streaming option this week against the Lions. After a heinous 2025 season, Smith has acquitted himself reasonably well this season while playing behind a competent Jets offensive line. Smith has completed 70.8% of his throws for 462 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions. The real appeal here is the opponent. The Saints’ Tyler Shough torched the Detroit defense for 410 passing yards and three TD passes in Week 1. The Bills’ Josh Allen threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns against the Lions in Week 2. I’m ranking Smith as a midrange QB2 against the Lions.

With Jonathon Brooks
on IR with a groin injury, Chuba Hubbard is poised to get ample work this week against the Browns. The Panthers’ offense has looked surprisingly potent early in the season, with Bryce Young playing at a level we’ve rarely seen from him since he entered the NFL. Hubbard isn’t extraordinarily talented, and Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland is where offense goes to die. Still, volume is volume, and Hubbard is a good bet for 15 or more touches this week. Consider him a midrange RB2.
The Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3, and Rico Dowdle
is questionable because of a toe injury. If Dowdle is out, Jaylen Warren becomes a must-start. The Pittsburgh offense has been dysfunctional this season, but Warren could be a frequent checkdown option for immobile 42-year-old QB Aaron Rodgers. Warren would also get the vast majority of Pittsburgh’s rushing attempts, and he’s been an efficient, underrated runner throughout his career.
Quinshon Judkins
has had 12 carries in each of his first two games and hasn’t had a run of 10 or more yards. He’s averaging 2.3 yards per carry behind a rebuilt Browns offensive line that ranks dead last in the run-blocking metric adjusted line yards. But Judkins gets a favorable home matchup against a Panthers defense that has given up the most rushing yards to RBs. Consider Judkins a low-end RB3.
The Patriots’ backfield got messy last week with the return of TreVeyon Henderson
from an ankle injury. Henderson had 16-76-1 rushing against the Steelers last week, with a 39-yard TD run. Henderson played 13 more snaps and had 10 more carries than Rhamondre Stevenson, possibly because Stevenson lost a fumble on New England’s first possession of the game. But Stevenson is regarded as the far better pass blocker, and the Patriots’ offensive line has not done a great job of handling pressure this season. It’s going to be very hard to predict the workload split between Henderson and Stevenson. I’m ranking Henderson as a high-end RB3 and Stevenson as a midrange RB3. They’re both reasonable flex options with unsteady floors.
Woody Marks
has played 49% of the Texans’ offensive snaps and has played only three fewer snaps than David Montgomery. Marks has had 23 touches over the Texans’ first two games. The Colts are an inviting matchup for RBs. I don’t think it’s possible to overstate how bad the Colts’ defense has been so far – particularly their linebackers. The Colts have allowed the second-most rushing yards and the second-most receiving yards to RBs. The combination of matchup and usage make Woody Marks a viable Week 3 flex play.

Adonai Mitchell
is currently WR35 in half-point PPR fantasy scoring, and he’s WR25 in expected fantasy points per game, according to Fantasy Points Data. Mitchell leads all NFL receivers in air yards share, having accounted for a whopping 59.4% of the Jets’ air yards. Mitchell has out-targeted teammate Garrett Wilson 15-14. Mitchell had 6-63-0 on a team-high 12 targets against the Packers in Week 2. In addition to his six catches, he drew a long pass interference penalty early in the game. Mitchell has a Week 3 matchup against a Lions defense that has allowed 658 passing yards and six TD passes. Detroit’s secondary is a disaster zone. Mitchell is a high-end WR3. Get him into lineups where you can.
Chris Olave
is second in the league in both catches and receiving yards. Olave is also tied for second with DK Metcalf in total routes run. And yet, Olave is actually second on his own team in routes run. Devaughn Vele leads all NFL receivers with 89 routes. Vele has 12 catches for 133 yards and one TD. The Saints have a high-volume passing game, and they have a weather-proof home matchup against the Raiders this week in the Caesars Superdome. Vele is an appealing midrange WR3.
On one hand, the absence of Alec Pierce
due to a heel injury enhances the target outlook for Josh Downs. On the other hand, the Texans are a tough matchup, even if the Houston defense hasn’t been lights-out over the first two weeks. Will Downs offer anything more than low-calorie PPR production? One positive for Downs is that he’s been in the slot on 78.9% of his snaps. I was worried that with Keenan Allen around, the Colts might have Downs line up outside more often. Downs is a little guy, and if cornerbacks can get their hands on him off the snap, it throws him off. Fortunately, Downs is still working mostly from the slot. I’m ranking Downs as a midrange WR3.
Ravens WR Zay Flowers
may or may not return from a hamstring injury this week. The guess here is that the Ravens play it safe with Flowers and hold him out another week. The Ravens-Cowboys game will be played in Rio de Janeiro, and there have been concerns about the field conditions. Rashod Bateman was Baltimore’s lead receiver in Flowers’ absence, going for 7-88-1 on nine targets. He ran a route on 89.2% of Lamar Jackson‘s dropbacks – very encouraging involvement. Consider Bateman a low-end WR2 if Flowers misses Week 3.
Dontayvion Wicks
has topped 70 receiving yards in each of his first two games with the Eagles, with 2-73-1 on four targets against the Commanders in Week 1 and 5-74-0 on six targets against the Titans in Week 2. Wicks played 90.9% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps in Week 1, but his snap share slipped to 70.1% in Week 2, with Wicks playing one fewer snap than rookie Makai Lemon. The Bears are a seemingly appealing Week 3 matchup for Wicks, although Chicago’s outside cornerbacks, Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson, are two of the team’s better defenders. Regard Wicks as a high-end WR4.
I’m benching Luther Burden
in a couple of leagues this week. Case Keenum is expected to start at QB for the Bears, and the Eagles are a tough matchup. It’s also concerning that Burden had a 57% snap share in Week 2 and played four fewer snaps than Khalif Raymond. It was reminiscent of early last season, when Burden was routinely getting out-snapped by Olamide Zaccheaus. But Burden was a rookie last year, so the slow ramp-up made some sense. We seemed to be getting a Burden breakout late last season, so why is he playing fewer snaps than Khalif Raymond? I have Burden ranked outside the top 40 at wide receiver this week.

Rules of Engagement
Don't change months of draft prep based on four quarters of football
Week 1 panic drops/adds are the #1 mistake
Waiver wire solves problems (injuries, byes, true roster holes) — it is NOT an upgrade mechanism
0-1 is not a problem. Low Week 1 score is not a problem. Underperformance is not necessarily a problem
A problem = injury to a starter you relied on, bye week, true roster hole
Activity ≠ accomplishment. Most waiver moves don't win leagues
Don't chase last week's points — find next week's breakout
Don't drop players you were high on all summer for one bad week
If you drafted rookies, hold them — don't rotate rookies weekly
Handcuff your own RBs at draft time — if you're now scrambling for Emmett Johnson as a Walker owner, you blew it at draft time
Context matters more than the pickup itself
Buy low / sell high is the #1 winning attribute
Depth charts reflect overall value, not matchup-dependent rankings
Usage (snaps, routes, targets) > box score, especially Wk1–3
Route participation is the key indicator
Game script affects RB values significantly
Week 1 is often a liar — need multiple weeks of data
Many teams didn't play starters in preseason; new/returning players need time
Stay the course generally; Week 13–14 is when you start panicking
Borderline WR3/Flex: lean higher-ceiling/lower-floor if you need points

GSE Computer Vision — How It Sees the Game 

 How the machine sees the game 
 The GSE computer-vision pipeline, stage by stage: what the camera captures, how pixels become tracklets, how tracklets become speed, routes and separation — and how those become film features the engine learns from. 

 demo uses simulated data 
 pipeline code is real — merged to main 
 film signals: uncalibrated · weight 0 · shadow only 

 01 The pipeline 
 One frame's journey from broadcast pixels to a row in the film shadow ledger. Every stage below maps to a real module in packages/prediction-engine . 

 STAGE 1 Capture watcher · OpenCV 
 The Windows watcher grabs broadcast frames on a schedule armed around game windows. Each frame is timestamped and queued with its game context. 
 in Live TV signal → frame grabber out Timestamped JPEG frames + game id 

 STAGE 2 Detect tracking/cv-detector-contract · yolo-adapter 
 A YOLO detector finds every player in each frame and draws a bounding box. Output is just boxes + confidence — no identities yet. The detector is a swappable boundary: any trained detector can drop in behind the same contract. 
 in One frame out ~22 detections: box (x, y, w, h) + confidence 

 STAGE 3 Track tracking/cv-tracklet-association 
 Association links this frame's boxes to last frame's boxes (IoU overlap, motion-aware gating). A box followed across frames becomes a tracklet — e.g. T-07 — a persistent ID with a position history. This is the moment "a player" exists to the machine. 
 in Per-frame detections out Tracklets: id, team side, frame-by-frame positions 

 STAGE 4 Stabilize tracking/cv-movement-primitive · cv-camera-compensation 
 The broadcast camera pans and zooms . Optical flow estimates that camera motion every frame pair and subtracts it , so a player's movement is real movement, not camera movement. Toggle it off in the demo below and watch the speed readings go insane — that's what this stage prevents. 
 in Raw tracklet pixel positions out Camera-compensated positions + camera motion field (dx, dy) 

 STAGE 5 Map to the field tracking/cv-homography · cv-field-lines · cv-field-landmarks 
 Yard lines are detected in the frame, a homography is fit, and every pixel position is projected into real-world meters on a goal-line-origin field model. From here on, everything is measured in yards and meters, not pixels. 
 in Compensated pixel positions out Field positions (xM, yM) per frame per tracklet 

 STAGE 6 Measure movement tracking/cv-movement-primitive · deriveMovementMetrics 
 From the meter-positions, per tracklet: distance traveled , top speed , average speed — plus the full per-frame speed series, which yields sprint curves like time-to-top-speed and directional velocity. 
 in Field positions over time out distanceM · topSpeedMs · avgSpeedMs · per-frame speed 

 STAGE 7 Understand the play perception/cv-play-segmentation · cv-formation-classify · cv-route-extract · cv-separation-metrics · cv-jersey-ocr 
 The stream is cut into plays ( pre-snap → snap → live → whistle ). Pre-snap alignment is classified into a formation . Each receiver's path is matched against 14 route templates (go, slant, out, dig, post, corner, curl, comeback, flat, wheel, screen, drag, seam, hitch) with a confidence score, break point and depth. At the break and catch, separation to the nearest defender is measured in yards. Jersey-number OCR maps tracklets to roster players. 
 in Tracklets + field positions for one play out Route name + confidence · break angle° · sep@break yd · sep@catch yd · formation · player id 

 STAGE 8 Learn (shadow) film-features/* · film-feature-adapter · film_shadow_ledger 
 Per-play measurements roll up into film features : a player's route mix, target share by formation, average separation; a team's run/pass tendency by down-and-distance, formation frequencies, play-action rate. These flow into the engine shadow-only, weight 0 — logged to the shadow ledger for calibration, never touching a published number until validated. 
 in Per-play perception outputs out Player/team film features → shadow ledger rows (weight 0) 

 02 What the camera sees — live demo 
 A simulated play, processed the way the real pipeline processes it. Watch receiver T-07 run a dig route while the machine detects, tracks, stabilizes, maps and measures — the metric readouts are computed live from his simulated tracklet, using the same math as deriveMovementMetrics , breakAngle and nearestDefender .

 Try this: turn camera compensation OFF mid-play while the camera is panning. The velocity vectors explode and the speed readout spikes — the camera's own motion is polluting every measurement. That is exactly the failure Stage 4 exists to prevent. 

 03 Every metric it pulls 
 The complete inventory, straight from the code — real field names, real units, grouped by the stage that produces them. This is the full answer to "what metrics are involved." 

 Movement — per tracklet, every play 
 From deriveMovementMetrics + the per-frame speed series. The raw material for everything speed-related. 

 m distanceM Total ground covered by the player during the play. Sprint distance, route distance, pursuit distance — all the same measurement. 
 m/s topSpeedMs The single fastest frame-to-frame speed — the player's sprint speed on that play. 
 m/s avgSpeedMs Mean speed across the play. Separates the burners from the guys who jog between bursts. 
 m/s @ 60fps Per-frame speed series Speed at every frame — the full sprint curve. From this: time from snap to top speed , acceleration phases, and the dip-and-reburst at a route break. 
 vector Directional velocity Speed plus heading per frame: how fast, and exactly which direction. This is what the arrows in the demo are. 
 px cameraMotion dx/dy How far the broadcast camera itself moved between frames — estimated by optical flow, then subtracted. A measurement of the measurement. 

 Routes — per receiver, per play 
 From classifyRoute : the receiver's path matched against 14 route templates. 

 14 classes Route name go · slant · out · dig · post · corner · curl · comeback · flat · wheel · screen · drag · seam · hitch — or unknown when nothing fits. 
 0–1 confidence Margin between the best and second-best template match. Low confidence means the route was improvised or messy. 
 yards depthYards How far downfield the route went — the number behind "he's their deep threat" vs "he lives underneath." 
 field point breakPoint The exact spot of maximum curvature — where the cut happened. Null on straight routes (go/seam have no break). 
 seconds releaseT When the receiver left the line relative to the snap — slow releases vs instant burners. 

 Separation — per route, per play 
 From cv-separation-metrics : the man-coverage truth serum. Nearest defender = closest opposing tracklet by field position. 

 degrees breakAngleDeg Angle between the incoming stem and the outgoing break — e.g. ~90° on a dig. Sharpness of the cut, measured, not eyeballed. 
 yards sepAtBreakYd Distance to the nearest defender at the break — did the cut actually create space? 
 yards sepAtCatchYd Distance to the nearest defender at the catch point — the contested-catch meter. 
 tracklet id nearestDefenderAtBreak Which defender was closest at the break — feeds matchup analysis (who got cooked, by whom). 

 Player film features — per player, rolling 
 From extractPlayerFilmFeatures : per-play measurements aggregated into a player profile. Needs the tracklet→player identity map — without it, these are skipped, never guessed. 

 shares routeMix Route name → share of the player's classified routes. His actual route tree, from film. 
 shares targetShareByFormation Where he lines up vs how often he's involved — formation tells you the plan. 
 yards avgSepAtBreakYd / avgSepAtCatchYd Does he separate consistently, or was one play a fluke? 
 deg / yards avgBreakAngleDeg / avgDepthYards How sharp his cuts are on average, how deep his average route goes. 
 share redZoneRouteShare Share of his routes run with the ball inside the opponent's 20 — red-zone role, measured. 

 Team film features + tendencies — per team, rolling 
 From extractTeamFilmFeatures and cv-tendencies : what the film says about the scheme. 

 matrix Down × distance run/pass Full 4-downs × short/medium/long run-pass tendency matrix. "They pass 78% on 2nd-and-long" — from film, not vibes. 
 shares formationFreq Personnel + distribution → share of plays. How often they live in 11 personnel, bunch, empty… 
 yards yardsPerPlayByFormation Which formations actually produce — scheme efficiency, measured per formation family. 
 rates playActionRate / screenRate / hurryUpRate How often they use play-action, screens, and tempo — the tendency fingerprints. 
 ranked list routeCombinationFrequency Most common route combos from each formation family — what the defense is actually defending. 
 label Formation classification Pre-snap alignment → personnel + distribution + play-action/screen/hurry-up flags, from cv-formation-classify . 

 04 One play, end to end 
 Trace a single snap through the whole machine — the same dig route from the demo above. 

 Capture Watcher grabs the broadcast at 60fps. Frame 1,142 lands with timestamp t=0.80s — the snap. 
 Detect YOLO returns 22 boxes. One of them: (x 612, y 388, w 26, h 40), conf 0.93 — a player, no name yet. 
 Track IoU association links it to the same box 59 frames running. It becomes tracklet T-07 , offense side. 
 Stabilize Camera panned 34px following the play. Optical flow measured it; every T-07 position is shifted back by the camera field. Without this, his speed would read 11.2 m/s. With it: 8.6. 
 Map Yard lines detected, homography fit. T-07's pixels become (36.6m, 11.0m) on the goal-line-origin field. 
 Measure distanceM 20.2 · topSpeedMs 8.6 · avgSpeedMs ~6.5 — plus the per-frame curve showing 0.75s from release to top speed and the gather-dip at the break. 
 Understand Segmented as one play, snap→whistle. Formation: 11 personnel, 2x2 . T-07's path matches the dig template at 0.87 confidence, depth 7.5 yd, break at (43.4m, 11.0m). Break angle 90.0°. Separation at break 2.3 yd (nearest: T-24). Separation at catch 1.1 yd. Jersey OCR reads #11 → roster identity attached. 
 Learn Rolled into the player's film profile (dig share up, avg separation updated) and the team's tendency matrix. Written to film_shadow_ledger as a weight-0 shadow row — visible to calibration, invisible to every published number. 

 Honest status — what this page is and isn't 

 The pipeline stages, module names and metric definitions are real — pulled from the merged code in packages/prediction-engine/src/{tracking,perception,film-features} today. 
 The animation is simulated — synthetic players on a synthetic field. It demonstrates the pipeline's logic (the speed math, break-angle math and separation math mirror the real functions); it is not real game footage and not real measurements. 
 Detector boundary: the repo holds the detector contract , not YOLO weights — a trained detector drops in behind it. 
 Identity gap: player-level film features need the tracklet→player map (jersey OCR + roster join). Until that lands, they are skipped, not guessed. 
 Calibration: every film signal is UNCALIBRATED, weight 0, shadow-only until the validation spec (PR #1003) is satisfied with real graded film. Nothing on this page touches a published projection. 
 Pipeline tests: 196/196 green on synthetic fixtures. Real-film validation is the next mountain.

title: EYI: build_video.py
body:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Galaxy Sports Edge - MNF Kelce recap video builder (1080x1920, 30fps).
Kelce-win ONLY. Original motion graphics only. No em dashes anywhere on screen.
"""
import math, subprocess, os
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageFilter

W, H, FPS = 1080, 1920, 30
OUT_DIR = "/home/hatch/workspace/your_files/mnf-recap-20260915"
AUDIO_DIR = f"{OUT_DIR}/audio_v2"
AUDIO = f"{AUDIO_DIR}/vo_final.mp3"
MP4 = f"{OUT_DIR}/mnf-recap.mp4"

def probe_dur(path):
    r = subprocess.run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration",
                        "-of", "csv=p=0", path], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return float(r.stdout.strip())

DURS = [probe_dur(f"{AUDIO_DIR}/c{i}.mp3") for i in range(1, 6)]
CHUNKS = []
s = 0.0
for d_ in DURS:
    CHUNKS.append((s, s + d_))
    s += d_
TAIL = 0.7
TOTAL = CHUNKS[-1][1] + TAIL
print("chunk durations:", DURS, "total:", TOTAL, flush=True)

# palette
BG = (4, 6, 16)
BLUE = (0, 212, 255)
PURPLE = (168, 85, 247)
GREEN = (46, 255, 150)
WHITE = (245, 247, 255)
MUTED = (150, 170, 210)
GOLD = (255, 200, 80)

def font(name, size):
    paths = [
        f"/usr/share/fonts/truetype/noto/{name}",
        f"/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/{name}",
    ]
    for p in paths:
        try:
            return ImageFont.truetype(p, size)
        except OSError:
            continue
    return ImageFont.load_default()

F_BLACK = lambda s: font("NotoSans-Black.ttf", s)
F_BOLD = lambda s: font("NotoSans-Bold.ttf", s)
F_REG = lambda s: font("NotoSans-Regular.ttf", s)

# ---------------- background: nebula + drifting stars ----------------
def make_nebula():
    img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img, "RGBA")
    def glow(cx, cy, r, color, alpha):
        for i in range(6):
            rr = int(r * (1 - i / 7))
            a = int(alpha * (1 - i / 6) / 6)
            d.ellipse([cx - rr, cy - rr, cx + rr, cy + rr], fill=color + (a,))
    glow(200, 420, 700, (10, 60, 140), 90)
    glow(950, 1500, 800, (90, 30, 150), 90)
    glow(700, 950, 500, (0, 90, 110), 50)
    vig = Image.new("L", (W, H), 0)
    vd = ImageDraw.Draw(vig)
    vd.ellipse([-W * 0.35, -H * 0.25, W * 1.35, H * 1.25], fill=255)
    vig = vig.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(220))
    black = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), (0, 0, 0))
    img = Image.composite(img, black, vig)
    return img

def make_stars(n, bright):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(n * 7919 + 13)
    layer = np.zeros((H, W), dtype=np.float32)
    xs = rng.integers(0, W, n)
    ys = rng.integers(0, H, n)
    layer[ys, xs] = rng.uniform(0.35, 1.0, n) * bright
    layer = np.stack([layer] * 3, axis=-1)
    tint = np.array([0.75, 0.85, 1.0], dtype=np.float32)
    return (layer * tint)

NEBULA = np.asarray(make_nebula()).astype(np.float32)
STARS_FAR = make_stars(220, 0.55)
STARS_NEAR = make_stars(90, 1.0)

def background(t):
    bg = NEBULA.copy()
    sf = int((t * 6) % H)
    sn = int((t * 16) % H)
    bg += np.roll(STARS_FAR, sf, axis=0) * 255
    bg += np.roll(STARS_NEAR, sn, axis=0) * 255
    return np.clip(bg, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

# ---------------- card factory ----------------
def ease_out_back(p):
    c1, c3 = 1.70158, 2.70158
    return 1 + (c3 * (p - 1) ** 3 + c1 * (p - 1) ** 2)

def draw_check(d, cx, cy, r, color, width=16):
    d.line([cx - r * 0.7, cy, cx - r * 0.15, cy + r * 0.55], fill=color, width=width, joint="curve")
    d.line([cx - r * 0.15, cy + r * 0.55, cx + r * 0.8, cy - r * 0.6], fill=color, width=width, joint="curve")

def make_stat_card(name, big, sub, accent, mark):
    """mark: 'check' | None. Returns RGBA image 920x560."""
    cw, chh = 920, 560
    card = Image.new("RGBA", (cw, chh), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(card)
    for i in range(3):
        d.rounded_rectangle([8 + i * 3, 8 + i * 3, cw - 8 - i * 3, chh - 8 - i * 3],
                            radius=44, outline=accent + (60 - i * 18,), width=6)
    d.rounded_rectangle([14, 14, cw - 14, chh - 14], radius=40, fill=(8, 12, 26, 232))
    d.rounded_rectangle([14, 14, cw - 14, chh - 14], radius=40, outline=accent + (255,), width=5)
    cx = cw // 2
    d.text((cx, 96), name, font=F_BOLD(56), fill=MUTED + (255,), anchor="mm")
    d.text((cx, 268), big, font=F_BLACK(170), fill=WHITE + (255,), anchor="mm",
           stroke_width=3, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0, 255))
    d.text((cx, 462), sub, font=F_BOLD(50), fill=accent + (255,), anchor="mm")
    if mark == "check":
        draw_check(d, cw - 108, 102, 46, GREEN + (255,), width=20)
    return card

def stamp_cashed():
    img = Image.new("RGBA", (620, 170), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    d.rounded_rectangle([6, 6, 614, 164], radius=26, outline=GOLD + (255,), width=8)
    d.text((310, 85), "CASHED", font=F_BLACK(84), fill=GOLD + (255,), anchor="mm")
    return img.rotate(-8, expand=True, resample=Image.BICUBIC)

def slam(frame, card_img, cx, cy, t0, t, extra=None):
    lt = t - t0
    if lt < 0:
        return
    if lt < 0.45:
        s = 0.5 + 0.5 * ease_out_back(lt / 0.45)
        alpha = min(1.0, lt / 0.18)
    else:
        s, alpha = 1.0, 1.0
    nw, nh = int(card_img.width * s), int(card_img.height * s)
    if nw < 2 or nh < 2:
        return
    c = card_img.resize((nw, nh), Image.LANCZOS)
    if alpha < 1.0:
        a = c.getchannel("A").point(lambda v: int(v * alpha))
        c.putalpha(a)
    ox, oy = 0, 0
    if 0.45 <= lt < 0.75:  # impact shake
        ts = lt - 0.45
        ox = int(11 * math.exp(-9 * ts) * math.sin(46 * ts))
        oy = int(7 * math.exp(-9 * ts) * math.cos(38 * ts))
    frame.alpha_composite(c, (int(cx - nw / 2 + ox), int(cy - nh / 2 + oy)))
    if extra == "ring" and 0 < lt < 0.6:
        p = lt / 0.6
        r = int(120 + 420 * p)
        a = int(160 * (1 - p))
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(frame, "RGBA")
        d.ellipse([cx - r, cy - r, cx + r, cy + r], outline=BLUE + (a,), width=10)

CARD_SCORE = make_stat_card("MONDAY NIGHT FINAL", "31 - 10", "CHIEFS  •  BRONCOS", BLUE, None)
CARD_CALL = make_stat_card("THE CALL", "38.5+", "KELCE RECEIVING YARDS", BLUE, None)
CARD_KELCE = make_stat_card("TRAVIS KELCE", "71", "YARDS. LINE WAS 38.5.", GREEN, "check")
STAMP = stamp_cashed()

def make_deal():
    img = Image.new("RGBA", (940, 440), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    d.text((470, 120), "PICKS GO UP", font=F_BLACK(92), fill=WHITE + (255,), anchor="mm",
           stroke_width=3, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0, 255))
    d.text((470, 210), "BEFORE KICKOFF.", font=F_BLACK(92), fill=WHITE + (255,), anchor="mm",
           stroke_width=3, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0, 255))
    d.text((470, 340), "RESULTS GET POSTED AFTER.", font=F_BLACK(58), fill=BLUE + (255,), anchor="mm",
           stroke_width=3, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0, 255))
    return img

DEAL = make_deal()

# end card
LOGO = Image.open("/home/hatch/workspace/vendor/autonomous-revenue-engine/brand/gse-logo-mark-2026-09-10.jpg").convert("RGB")
LOGO = LOGO.resize((460, 460), Image.LANCZOS)
_mask = Image.new("L", (460, 460), 0)
ImageDraw.Draw(_mask).rounded_rectangle([0, 0, 460, 460], radius=110, fill=255)
LOGO.putalpha(_mask)

def draw_endcard(frame, t):
    lt = t - CHUNKS[4][0]
    a = min(1.0, max(0.0, lt / 0.8))
    if a <= 0:
        return
    ov = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
    d.ellipse([W // 2 - 300, 560 - 300, W // 2 + 300, 560 + 300], outline=BLUE + (110,), width=6)
    ov.alpha_composite(LOGO, (W // 2 - 230, 560 - 230))
    d.text((W // 2, 1120), "GALAXY SPORTS EDGE", font=F_BLACK(66), fill=WHITE + (255,), anchor="mm")
    d.text((W // 2, 1200), "Every pick public. Every result posted.",
           font=F_REG(44), fill=MUTED + (255,), anchor="mm")
    if a < 1.0:
        al = ov.getchannel("A").point(lambda v: int(v * a))
        ov.putalpha(al)
    frame.alpha_composite(ov)

# ---------------- captions ----------------
PHRASES = [
    [("Monday night.", 0.00), ("Chiefs, thirty-one. Broncos, ten.", 0.30)],
    [("The call:", 0.00), ("Travis Kelce over thirty-eight", 0.28), ("and a half receiving yards.", 0.60)],
    [("The result: seventy-one.", 0.00), ("Nearly double.", 0.55)],
    [("Picks go up before kickoff.", 0.00), ("Results get posted after.", 0.40), ("That is the whole operation.", 0.66)],
    [("Galaxy Sports Edge.", 0.00), ("Back tomorrow.", 0.45)],
]

def wrap(text, fnt, max_w):
    words, lines, cur = text.split(), [], ""
    for w_ in words:
        t = (cur + " " + w_).strip()
        if fnt.getlength(t) <= max_w:
            cur = t
        else:
            lines.append(cur); cur = w_
    lines.append(cur)
    return lines

def draw_caption(frame, ci, t):
    s, e = CHUNKS[ci]
    frac = (t - s) / (e - s)
    phrases = PHRASES[ci]
    idx = 0
    for i, (_, f0) in enumerate(phrases):
        if frac >= f0:
            idx = i
    text, f0 = phrases[idx]
    f1 = phrases[idx + 1][1] if idx + 1 < len(phrases) else 1.0
    pop = min(1.0, (frac - f0) / max(0.001, (f1 - f0) * 0.25 + 0.02))
    sc = 0.88 + 0.12 * min(1.0, pop * 1.4)
    fnt = F_BOLD(58)
    lines = wrap(text, fnt, W - 140)
    lh = 78
    total_h = lh * len(lines)
    y0 = 1560 - total_h / 2
    tmp = Image.new("RGBA", (W, 420), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(tmp)
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        d.text((W / 2, 40 + i * lh), ln, font=fnt, fill=WHITE + (255,), anchor="mm",
               stroke_width=4, stroke_fill=(2, 3, 10, 255))
    nw, nh = int(W * sc), int(420 * sc)
    tmp = tmp.resize((nw, nh), Image.LANCZOS)
    frame.alpha_composite(tmp, ((W - nw) // 2, int(y0 - (nh - 420) / 2)))

def render_frame(t):
    frame = Image.fromarray(background(t), "RGB").convert("RGBA")
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(frame)
    d.text((W / 2, 96), "GALAXY SPORTS EDGE", font=F_BOLD(34), fill=(150, 170, 210, 150), anchor="mm")
    c0, c1 = CHUNKS[0][0], CHUNKS[0][1]
    if c0 <= t < c1:
        slam(frame, CARD_SCORE, W / 2, 780, c0 + 0.3, t, extra="ring")
        draw_caption(frame, 0, t)
    elif CHUNKS[1][0] <= t < CHUNKS[1][1]:
        slam(frame, CARD_CALL, W / 2, 780, CHUNKS[1][0] + 0.3, t, extra="ring")
        draw_caption(frame, 1, t)
    elif CHUNKS[2][0] <= t < CHUNKS[2][1]:
        slam(frame, CARD_KELCE, W / 2, 760, CHUNKS[2][0] + 0.3, t, extra="ring")
        lt = t - (CHUNKS[2][0] + 0.3)
        if lt > 2.2:
            s = 0.5 + 0.5 * ease_out_back(min(1.0, (lt - 2.2) / 0.4))
            st = STAMP.resize((int(STAMP.width * s), int(STAMP.height * s)), Image.LANCZOS)
            frame.alpha_composite(st, (W // 2 - st.width // 2, 1220))
        draw_caption(frame, 2, t)
    elif CHUNKS[3][0] <= t < CHUNKS[3][1]:
        slam(frame, DEAL, W / 2, 800, CHUNKS[3][0] + 0.3, t)
        draw_caption(frame, 3, t)
    else:
        draw_endcard(frame, t)
        draw_caption(frame, 4, t)
    return frame.convert("RGB")

def concat_audio():
    lst = f"{AUDIO_DIR}/concat.txt"
    with open(lst, "w") as f:
        for i in range(1, 6):
            f.write(f"file 'c{i}.mp3'\n")
    subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0",
                    "-i", lst, "-c", "copy", AUDIO], check=True, cwd=AUDIO_DIR)

def main():
    concat_audio()
    n = int(TOTAL * FPS)
    print(f"rendering {n} frames", flush=True)
    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error",
           "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "rgb24", "-s", f"{W}x{H}", "-r", str(FPS), "-i", "-",
           "-i", AUDIO,
           "-c:v", "libx264", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-crf", "18", "-preset", "medium",
           "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "160k", "-shortest", MP4]
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE)
    for i in range(n):
        t = i / FPS
        frame = render_frame(t)
        p.stdin.write(frame.tobytes())
        if i % 150 == 0:
            print(f"  frame {i}/{n}", flush=True)
    p.stdin.close()
    p.wait()
    print("done", MP4, flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
